topics.title: The Need for Smaller Units and A Tenth Part

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a unit is split into smaller equal parts to measure lengths more exactly.
Express and read lengths as units and one-tenths, and convert between mixed and tenths forms.
Add and subtract lengths in units and tenths, regrouping 10 tenths as 1 unit.
Relate one-hundredths to one-tenths and units and write lengths using hundredths.
Compare lengths written with tenths and hundredths.
Add and subtract quantities in units, tenths and hundredths with regrouping.
Explain how the Indian place value system is extended to tenths, hundredths and thousandths.
Write quantities given in units, tenths and hundredths in decimal notation.
Read decimal numbers correctly, digit by digit after the decimal point.
Convert between millimetres, centimetres and metres using decimals.
Convert between grams and kilograms using decimals.
Convert between paise and rupees using decimals.
Locate decimal numbers on a number line divided into equal parts.
Recognise that zeros on the right of the last decimal digit do not change the value.
Compare decimals place by place and find the decimal closest to a given number.
Add decimal numbers by aligning place values and regrouping.
Subtract decimal numbers by aligning place values and regrouping.
Identify the rule of a decimal sequence and extend it.
Explain how misplacing a decimal point or mixing units changes a quantity.
Interpret notations such as hours and cricket overs that look decimal but are not based on ten.
Recall key steps in the history of decimal notation and the decimal separator.
